label: 5 minutes
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Sanjay Gandhi, a Senior Software Engineer and Tech Lead at Oracle Healthcare, with over six years across Oracle, Google, Amazon, and HackerEarth.

At Oracle, I lead an 8-engineer Clinical Reporting team across 3 products. My major focus is Medical Record Output Generation, or MRO Gen2, which I built from 0 to 1. Its 7 microservices generate reports using different content types, data, and output formats. The platform handles more than 1M requests each day with p90 latency under 30 seconds.

XR and DEX are the Gen1 equivalents of MRO, and my team and I handle their KTLO work. I lead technical direction, architecture, delivery, and incident resolution. My major learnings have been mentoring engineers, creating effective processes, and owning microservices end to end. I work with 25+ cross-functional teams and helped reduce Gen2 onboarding from 2 weeks to under 1 week.

Before Oracle, I was part of Google Search and the Search India Education team. I built exam OSRPs and the interactive Exam Quiz, reaching 100M+ educational users on a product serving 1B+ queries per day. I launched localized education experiences, including the Periodic Table, in Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu.

One challenging Google project moved a Search experience from an entity-driven to an intent-driven architecture, helping the results page answer user intent directly. I worked across several languages in the Search monorepo, which has 2B+ lines of code and 10M+ files. That strengthened my ability to understand unfamiliar systems, debug at scale, and collaborate across teams.

My journey began during college. I explored different areas of computer science before focusing on competitive programming and machine learning. I solved more than 1,000 programming problems, reached World Rank 1 in a global contest, and learned from seniors who encouraged me to choose harder challenges.

In my third year, Amazon visited our campus to hire for a 9-month internship. I was fortunate to receive a direct full-time offer instead. At Amazon Finance Automation, I built statistical and machine-learning systems for invoice anomaly detection. Three rules identified more than 100M USD in anomalies in their first month, and our work reduced reporting latency from 24 hours to about 5 minutes.

Before joining Amazon full time, I worked at HackerEarth as a Problem Curator. I created and tested coding problems for hiring programs, including HackWithInfy, which served 167,000 participants. The role taught me that a good problem must measure the right skill and treat every candidate fairly. Teaching an advanced data structures workshop to 120+ attendees strengthened my own knowledge.

Mentoring remains important to me. I returned to college to help juniors prepare for placements, continued mentoring engineers at work, and regularly contribute to hiring. I serve as a Senior Key Interviewer and recognized Bar Raiser at Oracle, with more than 100 interviews and 25 hires.

The common thread has been solving difficult problems, learning quickly, and helping people grow. I’m now looking for greater leadership responsibility, broader technical ownership, and challenges where I can build reliable systems with meaningful impact.
